title: Always love a play that sticks the landing #homeplay #broadway #theat...
transcript: I went to go see the first play of the 2425 season, Roundabouts, Home. Home is a revival of the play that originally premiered on Broadway in 1979 by Sam Art Williams, who sadly passed away a few weeks before this revival opened. And home is part of the Roundabouts Refocus Project, which is their project to find overlooked works of art throughout history should be considered classics, and for whatever reason, aren't. And this is the perfect, perfect play to produce as part of that, because this is a play that I personally had never heard of, but is absolutely fantastic. Home follows the journey of Cephus Miles, a black man growing up in rural Crossroads, North Carolina, as he finds love and loss and stands up for what he believes in and ultimately tries to find home. The narrative style of this play took me a while to get into. This is really formulated like a what I like to call the one man show with an ensemble, where you have the one central figure here, see for smiles, played by Tory Kittles, and then two ensemble members, that's these two women who end up playing all of the characters in his life. It's also very word of mouth storytelling, so it's like they are telling you, the audience, this story directly. There's a lot of fourth wall breaking in this, and that took me a while to get used to, but after I was in it, it hooked Me perfectly. I definitely don't think that this is going to be a play for everyone because of the writing style and the narrations style. There were moments where I felt disengaged from material. For every moment that I felt disengaged, there was a moment that would bring me back in. Either a really clever bit of humor or, um, a piece of music. There's some. Some singing in this that always brings me back in. And ultimately, the payoff was worth it because the ending of this play is just so good. What a play that sticks the landing. I'm really glad I saw this. I thought the performances were stellar. A lot of really great character work in this. Um, really love the design. I don't always love Kenny Leon's direction, but for. For me, this is one of the shows that I really liked the most of his work. And I would definitely recommend this if you wanna see a play that takes you on a truly a journey. Far as tickets go, I did get my ticket. They were doing a pay what you want program, uh, with the code return home. I don't know if that's still good, but if you want to get pay what you want tickets, that is an option. If that's not available still, they also have hip tics available because this is a roundabout production, for $30. And if you don't qualify for hip tics, they also have an In person, rush. There's a lot of different ways to get tickets to this that are definitely affordable. Home is, in fact, the most affordable show on Broadway right now. This is also a very limited run, so you only have until July 21st to go see home. But definitely catch it if you can.
